description:
`c_int`, `cstring` and `unit` are wire-only spellings: the contract the type checker sees is rewritten to the semantic spelling by `normalize_extern_semantic_body` (src/extern_contract.rs), which only rewrites a body that is ONE token. So a spelling written inside an aggregate -- `extern "C" defp f() :: {c_int, integer}` -- survives normalization and `resolve_spec_decl` reports `compiler2 could not resolve extern contract for \`f\`: unknown type name \`c_int\``.

The refusal is correct (a pair field rides a whole return register, and `ty_to_extern_ty` can only ever produce I64/F64/Bool for one) and it reaches every door identically. The MESSAGE is wrong: `c_int` is a documented spelling, so "unknown type name" sends the reader looking for a typo instead of telling them the spelling is only valid as a whole parameter or result.

Found while building fz-21x.12; pre-existing for `cstring` and `unit`. A fix needs an error channel out of `extern_semantic_contract`, which today returns `Option` and is read by both `jobs/contract.rs` and `jobs/body.rs`.
title: A wire-only spelling inside an aggregate reports `unknown type name`
